mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Let's start with the markets. Stocks split sharply on Tuesday. The Dow rose 423 points, or 0.85 percent, to close at 50,019, finishing above 50,000 for the first time. The S&P 500 slipped half a percent to 7,201, its eighth loss in nine sessions, and the Nasdaq fell 1.48 percent. Chip stocks led the decline, with Nvidia dropping nearly 6 percent and Micron down about 11 percent, as worries about a December rate hike weighed on the AI trade. Health care was the best performing sector, and the 10 year Treasury yield ended near 4.9 percent. On the Fed, markets now see a rate hike at the December 9 meeting as very likely. Prediction markets and futures pricing put the odds of a quarter point increase at roughly 93 to 96 percent, up from about a third in late August. New York Fed President John Williams has recently said inflation remains too high. Today, the Fed releases its Beige Book survey of regional economic conditions at 2 p.m. Eastern, and Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman speaks this morning on banking supervision. Next, Sanofi agreed to buy biotech company Insmed for about 41 billion dollars in cash, or 175 dollars per share. Insmed shares rose about 14 percent, and the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Next, retailers had a strong day. Kohl's jumped about 19 percent after posting its first positive comparable sales in four years and raising its full year outlook. Abercrombie and Fitch, Dick's Sporting Goods, and Dollar Tree also rallied on better than expected results, and Best Buy rose after its best same store sales growth in five years. Next, Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell about 16 percent even though it beat estimates and raised guidance, as it flagged lower margins in its cloud and AI business. And finally, Dell reported record quarterly revenue of about 55 billion dollars after the bell, and its shares rose around 4 percent in after hours trading following an almost 12 percent drop during the regular session. On the calendar today, a heavy dose of data arrives at 8:30 a.m. Eastern ahead of Thanksgiving: the second estimate of third quarter GDP, October PCE inflation, personal income and spending, durable goods orders, and weekly jobless claims. New home sales follow at 10 a.m. Deere and Li Auto report earnings before the open. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday. Here's your fun fact. When World War One broke out in 1914, the New York Stock Exchange shut its doors on July 31 and stayed closed for more than four months, the longest trading suspension in its history. Bond trading resumed in late November, and stocks did not trade on the exchange floor again until December 12. In the meantime, brokers quietly traded shares out on the sidewalk of New Street. Have a great day.
